lecture.title: Coronary Artery Disease Part I (Chronic Coronary Syndrome)
golden_tip: EXAM TRAP: Acute coronary syndromes arise from rupture/erosion of plaques that are often < 50% stenosed — the vulnerable plaque, not the tightest one. Atherosclerosis stays asymptomatic until stenosis exceeds 70-80% of luminal diameter.
A NORMAL resting ECG does NOT exclude ischaemia, and a NORMAL resting echocardiogram does NOT exclude CAD — both are often normal between episodes in chronic coronary syndrome.

Exercise ECG excludes LVH, LBBB, resting ST depression and digoxin users. Best use: intermediate-risk/atypical or low-risk/typical patients. Sensitivity 68%, specificity 70%; stress echo accuracy 80-90%.

Statin rule for CCS: high-intensity statin for ALL regardless of baseline LDL, targeting LDL-C < 1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) AND a >= 50% reduction from baseline — add ezetimibe, then bempedoic acid, if the goal is unmet.

Revascularisation has a proven SURVIVAL benefit for left main stem (LMS), three-vessel disease, and LV systolic dysfunction — otherwise PCI/CABG in stable angina is for symptoms despite optimal medical therapy or patient preference.

concepts.title: Atherosclerosis: Plaque Biology and the CCS-ACS Spectrum
concepts.summary_ar: تصلب الشرايين: تسلسل تطور اللويحة من الخط الدهني إلى اللويحة الممزقة، ودور التمزق/التآكل في المتلازمتين المزمنة والحادة، وجدول المظاهر السريرية-المرضية.

sections.heading: Plaque Progression (from Fatty Streak to Rupture)
sections.body_text:
**Atherosclerosis begins with endothelial dysfunction**, then progresses through a stereotyped histological sequence (lecture table, from 'Sequences in progression of atherosclerosis'):

- **Fatty streak (earliest onset):** mainly **intracellular lipid accumulation** (foam cells) — **clinically silent**.
- **Intermediate lesion:** intracellular lipid accumulation plus **small extracellular lipid pools**.
- **Atheroma:** intracellular lipid accumulation with a **core of extracellular lipid**.
- **Fibroatheroma:** increased extracellular matrix/Smooth muscle cell accumulation — established lesion.
- **Vulnerable plaque: thin-cap fibroatheroma with a necrotic debris core** (rich in macrophage foam cells, dendritic cells and T cells with ApoB-lipoproteins).
- **Ruptured plaque (or eroded plaque): exposure of the thrombogenic core -> luminal thrombosis.**

**The coronary circulation segments (FIGURE 273-1):** **epicardial arteries > 400 micrometre (transport)**, **small arteries < 400 micrometre (regulation)**, **arterioles < 100 micrometre and capillaries < 10 micrometre (exchange)** — with most resistance normally in the microcirculation; microvascular dysfunction is a real cause of ischaemia.

**Ischaemia cascade (FIGURE 273-2):** decreased **subendocardial perfusion -> altered metabolism/abnormal ST -> micro-infarction/myocardial fibrosis**, as near-term or prolonged manifestations of an oxygen supply-demand mismatch, driven by **endothelial and microvascular dysfunction**.
key_points: Endothelial dysfunction initiates atherosclerosis
Fatty streak (silent) -> intermediate -> atheroma -> fibroatheroma -> vulnerable -> ruptured plaque
Vulnerable plaque: necrotic core, inflammatory cells, thin cap
Epicardial >400 um transport; small arteries <400 um regulation; arterioles/capillaries exchange
Ischaemia cascade: subendocardial hypoperfusion -> metabolic/ST changes -> micro-infarction/fibrosis

sections.heading: Role of Plaque Rupture and Erosion: CCS versus ACS
sections.body_text:
**Atherosclerosis is generally asymptomatic until the plaque stenosis exceeds 70 or 80 percent of the luminal diameter**, which can reduce flow and produce **typical angina pectoris**.

**Progression involves two distinct processes:**
- **A chronic process leading to slow luminal narrowing = chronic coronary syndrome (CCS).**
- **An acute process causing rapid luminal obstruction associated with plaque haemorrhage and/or luminal thrombosis = acute coronary syndrome (ACS).**

**Acute coronary and cerebrovascular syndromes (unstable angina, myocardial infarction, sudden death, and stroke) are typically due to RUPTURE or EROSION of plaques leading to thrombosis — although these plaques may have less than 50 percent stenosis.**

**Box 16.36 — CAD clinical manifestations and their pathology:**
| Clinical problem | Pathology |
|---|---|
| **Stable angina** | Ischaemia due to **fixed atheromatous stenosis** of one or more coronary arteries |
| **Unstable angina** | Ischaemia caused by **dynamic obstruction** due to **plaque rupture or erosion with superimposed thrombosis** |
| **Myocardial infarction** | **Myocardial necrosis** from acute occlusion (rupture/erosion + thrombosis) |
| **Heart failure** | Myocardial dysfunction due to infarction or ischaemia |
| **Arrhythmia** | Altered conduction due to ischaemia or infarction |
| **Sudden death** | Ventricular arrhythmia, asystole or massive myocardial infarction |
key_points: Silent until stenosis >70-80% luminal diameter
CCS = chronic slow narrowing; ACS = plaque haemorrhage/thrombosis with rapid obstruction
ACS lesions often <50% stenosed (rupture/erosion)
Stable angina = fixed stenosis; unstable = dynamic obstruction with thrombus

check.prompt: Why can a plaque of only 40% stenosis cause a myocardial infarction?
options: All plaques over 30% occlude eventually
Plaque rupture or erosion with superimposed thrombosis can rapidly convert a subcritical stenosis into total occlusion
Stenosis percentage does not relate to flow at all
Because plaques never rupture above 70%
check.explanation_ar: الاحتشاء لا يحتاج تضيقاً حرجاً مسبقاً: تمزق/تآكل اللويحة مع خثرة فائقة يحدث انسداداً سريعاً كاملاً؛ فالمتلازمات الحادة تنشأ غالباً من لويحات <50% (الهشة) لا من الأشد تضيقاً.

key_terms.definition_ar: لويحة قليلة التليف غنية بنخر التهابي وقبعة رقيقة؛ قابلة للتمزق وإحداث أحداث حادة.
تآكل سطح لويحة دون قلعة تليفية كاملة مع خثرة ملتصقة؛ آلية بديلة للتمزق في المتلازمات الحادة.

concepts.title: Risk Factors and the Myocardial Oxygen Supply-Demand Balance
concepts.summary_ar: عوامل خطر الشريان التاجي (جدول 8.1) غير المعدلة والمعدلة والواسمات، وصندوق 16.38 لعوامل ميزان أكسجة العضلة عرضاً وطلباً.

sections.heading: Risk Factors and Markers (TABLE 8.1)
sections.body_text:
**Non-modifiable risk factors:**
- **Age**
- **Male sex**
- **Family history of premature coronary artery disease**

**Modifiable independent risk factors:**
- **Hyperlipidaemia**
- **Hypertension**
- **Diabetes mellitus**
- **Metabolic syndrome**
- **Cigarette smoking**
- **Obesity**
- **Sedentary lifestyle**
- **Heavy alcohol intake**

**Markers (associated, not established as causal):**
- **Elevated lipoprotein(a)**
- **Hyperhomocysteinaemia**
- **Elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP)**
key_points: Non-modifiable: age, male sex, family history of premature CAD
Modifiable: lipids, BP, diabetes, metabolic syndrome, smoking, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, heavy alcohol
Markers: Lp(a), homocysteine, hsCRP

sections.heading: Myocardial Oxygen Supply and Demand (Box 16.38)
sections.body_text:
**Oxygen demand — determined by cardiac work:**
- **Heart rate**
- **Blood pressure**
- **Myocardial contractility**
- **Left ventricular hypertrophy**
- **Valve disease**

**Oxygen supply — determined by coronary blood flow** (which **occurs mainly in diastole**):
- **Duration of diastole** (the longer the diastole, the more coronary filling)
- **Coronary perfusion pressure (aortic diastolic minus coronary sinus or right atrial diastolic pressure)**
- **Coronary vasomotor tone**
- **Oxygenation: haemoglobin and oxygen saturation**

This balance explains both the physiology of angina (demand exceeding supply across a fixed stenosis) and the logic of every antianginal drug: **beta-blockers slow the heart rate (longer diastole, less demand); nitrates reduce preload/afterload (less demand) and dilate coronaries (more supply); calcium channel blockers reduce BP and contractility.**
key_points: Demand: heart rate, BP, contractility, LVH, valve disease
Supply: diastole duration, perfusion pressure (aortic diastolic - RA/coronary sinus diastolic), vasomotor tone, Hb/O2 saturation
Coronary blood flow occurs mainly in DIASTOLE
Every antianginal class maps onto this balance

key_terms.definition_ar: فرق الضغط الانبساطي الأبهري عن الضغط الانبساطي الأذيني الأيمن/الجيب التاجي؛ محدد التدفق التاجي.

concepts.title: Clinical Assessment of Suspected Stable Angina
concepts.summary_ar: التقويم السريري للذبحة المستقرة: الأعراض، الفحص الفيزيائي، الأشكال الخاصة (تشنجية، متلازمة X، ANOCA)، وترتيب الخطورة (16.41).

sections.heading: Symptoms and Physical Examination
sections.body_text:
**Symptoms of CAD:** chest pain (typical vs atypical), dyspnoea, palpitation, syncope — with the key distinctions of **unstable angina vs stable angina (CCS)** and the **angina equivalent** concept.

**Physical examination is frequently unremarkable** but should include a careful search for:
- **Evidence of valve disease (particularly aortic).**
- **Important risk factors: hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidaemia.**
- **Signs of left ventricular dysfunction.**
- **Other manifestations of arterial disease (carotid bruits, peripheral arterial disease).**
- **Unrelated conditions that may exacerbate angina: anaemia, thyrotoxicosis.**

**Special angina syndromes:**
- **Coronary artery spasm:** angina from **vasospasm**, which may coexist with atherosclerosis (especially in unstable angina) or occur as an **isolated phenomenon in less than 1% of cases with normal coronary arteries on angiography** — 'variant angina'; with **transient ST elevation** it is **Prinzmetal's angina**.
- **Syndrome X:** the constellation of **typical angina on effort + objective evidence of myocardial ischaemia on stress testing + normal coronary arteries on angiography**; many are **women**, mechanism often unclear, disorder poorly understood — **good prognosis but may respond to anti-anginal therapy**.
- **ANOCA/microvascular angina:** **one-third of patients may have no significant epicardial disease and often have microvascular disease as the underlying pathophysiology (angina with no obstructive coronary artery disease).**
- **Other causes of angina:** aortic stenosis, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and aortitis; rarely vasculitis.
key_points: Exam often unremarkable: seek valve disease (aortic), risk factors, LV dysfunction, carotid bruits/PAD, anaemia/thyrotoxicosis
Variant/Prinzmetal: isolated spasm <1%, normal coronaries, transient ST elevation
Syndrome X: typical effort angina + objective ischaemia + normal angiogram; women; good prognosis
One-third of angina patients have ANOCA (microvascular disease)
Angina also in AS, HOCM, aortitis

check.prompt: A 54-year-old woman has classic exertional chest tightness, a positive exercise ECG for ischaemia, and completely normal coronary arteries at angiography. What is this called?
options: Prinzmetal's angina
Syndrome X
Unstable angina
Aortic stenosis angina
check.explanation_ar: متلازمة X: ذبحة نموذجية مجهودية + دليل موضوعي لنقص التروية + شرايين طبيعية بالتصوير؛ شائعة لدى النساء ومآلها جيد وقد تستجيب للعلاج المضاد للذبحة — بينما برنزميتال تشنج مع ارتفاع ST عابر.

sections.heading: Risk Stratification in Stable Angina (Box 16.41)
sections.body_text:
**HIGH-risk features:**
- **Post-infarct angina**
- **Poor effort tolerance**
- **Ischaemia at low workload**
- **Left main or three-vessel disease**
- **Poor left ventricular function**

**LOW-risk features:**
- **Predictable exertional angina**
- **Good effort tolerance**
- **Ischaemia only at high workload**
- **Single-vessel or two-vessel disease**
- **Good left ventricular function**

This stratification directs both the **intensity of investigation (early imaging versus invasive strategy)** and the **urgency of considering revascularisation** — high-risk patients warrant definitive coronary imaging and, where anatomy confers survival benefit, revascularisation.
key_points: High risk: post-infarct angina, poor effort tolerance, low-workload ischaemia, left main/3VD, poor LV function
Low risk: predictable exertional angina, good tolerance, high-workload ischaemia only, 1-2 vessel disease, good LV

key_terms.definition_ar: ذبحة دون مرض تاجي إبكليلي انسادي؛ جذر المشكلة وعائي دقيق غالباً.
ذبحة نموذجية مع نقص تروية موضوعي وشرايين سليمة؛ شائعة بالنساء ومآل جيد.

concepts.title: Investigations: ECG, Echocardiography, Stress Testing and Coronary Imaging
concepts.summary_ar: التحقيقات في الذبحة المستقرة: التحاليل والتخطيط الأساسي والصدى السكوني، مبدأ اختبارات الجهد وطرقها واسترجاعها، والتصوير التاجي بالطبقي والقسطرة.

sections.heading: Baseline Tests: Bloods, ECG and Resting Echocardiography
sections.body_text:
**Blood tests:** **CBC, RBS (random blood sugar), HbA1c, RFT (renal function), lipid profile.**

**Baseline electrocardiogram (ECG)** may show:
- **ST-depression; T-wave inversion; pathological Q-waves.**
- Other abnormalities such as **ventricular hypertrophy, bundle branch block.**
- **A normal ECG does NOT exclude ischaemia** as the aetiology of chest pain.

**Resting echocardiography** provides useful information in the overall assessment of suspected stable angina (**to guide treatment options and for risk stratification**):
1. **Regional wall motion abnormalities.**
2. **LV systolic function (EF) may guide the choice of medical therapy versus revascularisation.**
3. **LV hypertrophy, assessment of the aortic (AS) and mitral (MR) valves.**
- **A NORMAL resting echocardiogram does NOT exclude CAD.**
key_points: Bloods: CBC, glucose/HbA1c, renal function, lipids
ECG: ST depression, T inversion, pathological Q, LVH, BBB — normal ECG does not exclude ischaemia
Echo: regional wall motion, EF (medical vs revascularisation), LVH, AS/MR — normal echo does not exclude CAD

sections.heading: Stress Testing: Inducing and Detecting Ischaemia
sections.body_text:
**Basic principle of stress testing: provoke ischaemia, followed by functional assessment with different modalities to detect it.** Stress tests are categorised by the methods used to **provoke** and to **detect** myocardial ischaemia.

**Methods to INDUCE ischaemia:**
- **Exercise** — the most physiologically sound and useful method; a test is **adequate if 85% or more of the age-predicted maximum heart rate (220 minus age) is achieved**, and it provides an **objective assessment of functional capacity with prognostic value**.
- **Pharmacological testing — dobutamine, adenosine or dipyridamole** — for patients who cannot exercise to an adequate heart rate.

**Methods to DETECT ischaemia:**
- **Stress ECG**
- **Stress echocardiography**
- **Nuclear study (SPECT, PET)**
- **CMR (stress perfusion MRI)**

**Stress ECG specifics:**
- **Exclude patients with LVH, LBBB, resting ST-depression, or those taking digoxin** (uninterpretable baseline).
- **Sensitivity 68% and specificity 70%** for the general population (lower in low-risk persons).
- **Best used in the INTERMEDIATE-risk patient with an atypical history, or the low-risk patient with a typical history** — the likelihood that an abnormal result indicates CAD is much higher for an older person with multiple risk factors.
- For most **high-risk** patients, **invasive testing is preferred** for definitive diagnosis and possible intervention.
- **Fig. 16.57 example:** resting ECG with minor inferolateral T-wave changes; after 3 minutes of treadmill exercise, **marked planar ST depression in V5 and V6** — angiography revealed **critical three-vessel disease**.

**Stress echocardiography:** accuracy in detecting significant coronary stenosis is **80-90%, superior to exercise electrocardiography** (new or worsening regional wall-motion abnormality at stress compared with rest).

**Nuclear study (SPECT): a perfusion defect present during stress but NOT at rest provides evidence of REVERSIBLE myocardial ischaemia.**

**Coronary artery imaging:** **CT coronary angiography** (non-invasive, also useful in the Fig. 16.55 pathway for patients without known CAD) and **invasive coronary artery catheterisation** (for high-risk patients or when revascularisation is planned — for patients with KNOWN CAD, further stress imaging rather than CTCA is recommended).
key_points: Adequate exercise test: >=85% of (220 - age); functional capacity has prognostic value
Pharmacological stress: dobutamine, adenosine, dipyridamole
Detection: stress ECG, stress echo, SPECT/PET, CMR
Stress ECG exclusions: LVH, LBBB, resting ST depression, digoxin; sens 68%/spec 70%
Stress echo accuracy 80-90%, superior to exercise ECG
Reversible perfusion defect (stress, not rest) = ischaemia on SPECT
CTCA for patients without known CAD; catheterisation for high-risk/known CAD

check.prompt: Which patients should be excluded from diagnostic exercise-ECG stress testing?
options: Patients with typical angina only
Patients with LVH, LBBB, resting ST-depression, or taking digoxin
Patients over 60
Patients with hyperlipidaemia
check.explanation_ar: خط الأساس غير القابل للتأويل (LVH، LBBB، انحراف ST راحة، ديجوكسين) يُخرج المريض من اختبار الجهد الكهربائي؛ البدائل: صدى الجهد أو التصوير النووي.

key_terms.definition_ar: بلوغ ≥85% من المعدل الأقصى المتوقع للعمر (220-العمر) قبل الحكم على سلبية الاختبار.
عيب تروية بالجهد يزول بالراحة؛ دليل نقص التروية في SPECT.
ذبحة بلا مرض انسدادي إبكليلي — ثلث المرضى؛ الآلية وعائية دقيقة غالباً.

concepts.title: Management I: Lifestyle, Risk-Factor Control, Antiplatelets, Statins and Antianginal Drugs
concepts.summary_ar: إدارة المتلازمة التاجية المزمنة: نصائح نمط الحياة (16.42)، ضبط الضغط والسكري، الأسبرين والستاتينات بأهداف LDL-C، وكل فئات مضادات الذبحة بجرعاتها.

sections.heading: Lifestyle, Hypertension, Diabetes, Antiplatelet and Statin Therapy
sections.body_text:
**Box 16.42 Advice to patients with stable angina:**
- **Do not smoke.**
- **Aim for an ideal body weight.**
- **Take regular exercise** (exercise up to, but not beyond, the point of chest discomfort is beneficial and **may promote collateral vessels**).
- **Avoid severe unaccustomed exertion, and vigorous exercise after a heavy meal or in very cold weather.**
- **Take a sublingual nitrate before undertaking exertion that may induce angina** (prophylactic use).

**Control of hypertension and diabetes (2024/2025 guidance as taught):**
- **In adults with CCD and hypertension (systolic BP >= 130 and/or diastolic BP >= 80 mmHg): ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-receptor blockers (ARB) or beta-blockers are recommended as FIRST-LINE therapy.**
- **In patients with CCD and type 2 diabetes (target HbA1c < 7.0%): an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist has proven cardiovascular benefit.**

**Antiplatelet therapy:**
- **All patients with angina secondary to CAD should receive antiplatelet therapy.**
- **Low-dose aspirin (75 mg) for all, continued indefinitely** (reduces MI risk).
- **Clopidogrel 75 mg daily is an equally effective alternative** if aspirin causes dyspepsia or other side effects.

**Statin therapy:**
- **All patients should be prescribed a statin, even if cholesterol is normal — evidence-based doses of a HIGH-INTENSITY statin regardless of baseline LDL.**
- **LDL-C goal: < 1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) AND a >= 50% reduction from baseline (Class I, Level A).**
- **Statin-intolerant patients not at goal on ezetimibe: add bempedoic acid (Class I B; IIa with maximally tolerated statin + ezetimibe).**
- **Intensity table:** HIGH (>= 50% LDL lowering): **atorvastatin 40-80 mg, rosuvastatin 20-40 mg**; MODERATE (30-49%): atorvastatin 10-20 mg, rosuvastatin 5-10 mg, simvastatin 20-40 mg, pravastatin 40-80 mg, lovastatin 40 mg, fluvastatin XL 80 mg; LOW (< 30%): simvastatin 10 mg, pravastatin 10-20 mg, fluvastatin 20-40 mg, pitavastatin 1-4 mg.
key_points: Advice: stop smoking, ideal weight, regular exercise (collaterals), avoid heavy-meal/cold-weather exertion, prophylactic GTN
HTN >=130/80: ACEi/ARB or beta-blocker first line
T2DM with CCD: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA (HbA1c <7.0%)
Aspirin 75 mg indefinitely; clopidogrel 75 mg if intolerant
High-intensity statin regardless of baseline LDL; goal LDL-C <1.4 mmol/L + >=50% reduction
Add ezetimibe then bempedoic acid if unmet
High intensity: atorvastatin 40-80, rosuvastatin 20-40

sections.heading: Antianginal Drugs (2024 ESC Recommendations and Davidson's Detail)
sections.body_text:
**Goal of anti-anginal therapy: control symptoms with the simplest regimen that does not cause side effects.** Five groups are available with little evidence that one is more effective than another; conventional start: **sublingual GTN + beta-blocker, then add a calcium channel antagonist or long-acting nitrate; if two drugs fail, consider revascularisation.**

**2024 ESC recommendations:**
- **Tailor antianginal selection to patient characteristics, comorbidities, concomitant medications, tolerability and the underlying pathophysiology (I C).**
- **Short-acting nitrates for immediate relief of angina (I B).**
- **Initial treatment with beta-blockers and/or CCBs to control heart rate and symptoms for most patients with CCS (I B).**
- **If not controlled on a beta-blocker or CCB alone: combination of beta-blocker + DHP-CCB (IIa B).**
- **Long-acting nitrates or ranolazine as add-on therapy for inadequate control on beta-blockers and/or CCBs (IIa B).**

**1. Nitrates** — act directly on vascular smooth muscle producing **venous and arteriolar dilatation**: they help angina by **lowering preload and afterload (reduced oxygen demand) and increasing supply through coronary vasodilatation**.
- **Sublingual GTN** (metered-dose aerosol **400 micrograms per spray**, or tablets 500/800 micrograms) relieves an attack in **2-3 minutes**; use **prophylactically** before exertion. Side effects: headache, symptomatic hypotension, rarely syncope.
- **Long-acting:** transcutaneous GTN patch **5-10 mg daily**; slow-release buccal **1-5 mg four times daily**; oral **isosorbide dinitrate 10-20 mg three times daily** or **isosorbide mononitrate 20-60 mg once or twice daily** (unlike GTN, not extensively first-pass metabolised).
- **Continuous nitrate therapy causes pharmacological tolerance — avoid with a 6-8-hour nitrate-free period, best at night**; if **nocturnal angina** predominates, give long-acting nitrates at the end of the day instead.

**2. Beta-blockers** — lower myocardial oxygen demand by **reducing heart rate, BP and myocardial contractility**; may provoke bronchospasm in asthma; theoretically non-selective agents may aggravate coronary vasospasm (blocked beta2-adrenoceptors).
- Prefer **once-daily cardioselective preparations: slow-release metoprolol 60-200 mg daily or bisoprolol 5-15 mg daily.**
- **Do NOT withdraw abruptly — the beta-blocker withdrawal syndrome can precipitate dangerous arrhythmias, worsening angina or MI.**

**3. Calcium channel antagonists** — lower oxygen demand by **reducing BP and myocardial contractility**.
- **Dihydropyridines (nifedipine, amlodipine) may cause reflex tachycardia — combine with a beta-blocker.**
- **Verapamil and diltiazem can be used as monotherapy** (slow SA node firing, inhibit AV conduction, bradycardia) — particularly useful when beta-blockers are contraindicated.
- **Caution in poor LV function** (negative inotropy can precipitate heart failure); other effects: peripheral oedema, flushing, headache, dizziness.
- **Box 16.44:** nifedipine 5-20 mg three times daily (marked tachycardia; slow-release preparations available); nicardipine 20-40 mg TID (less myocardial depression); amlodipine 2.5-10 mg daily (ultra-long-acting); verapamil 40-80 mg TID (constipation; anti-arrhythmic); diltiazem 60-120 mg TID (similar anti-arrhythmic properties).

**4. Potassium channel activators** — **nicorandil 10-30 mg twice daily orally**, the only drug in this class: **arterial and venous vasodilator without the tolerance seen with nitrates.**

**5. Other drugs:**
- **Ivabradine (If-channel antagonist):** induces **bradycardia by modulating sinus-node ion channels; does not inhibit myocardial contractility and appears safe in heart failure.**
- **Ranolazine:** inhibits the **late inward sodium current** in coronary artery smooth muscle cells (secondary effect on calcium flux and vascular tone), reducing angina symptoms.
key_points: Start GTN + beta-blocker; add CCB or long-acting nitrate; revascularise if two drugs fail
Short-acting nitrate = immediate relief (I B); beta-blocker and/or CCB initial therapy (I B)
Sublingual GTN 400 mcg spray/500-800 mcg tablet; relief in 2-3 min; prophylactic use
Nitrate tolerance: 6-8 h nitrate-free interval (at night)
Cardioselective BB: metoprolol SR 60-200 mg, bisoprolol 5-15 mg; no abrupt withdrawal
DHP-CCB with BB (reflex tachycardia); verapamil/diltiazem monotherapy; caution poor LV
Nicorandil 10-30 mg BD (K-channel activator, no nitrate tolerance)
Ivabradine: sinus-node If channel, HF-safe; ranolazine: late inward sodium current

check.prompt: Why is a nitrate-free interval prescribed for patients on continuous nitrate therapy?
options: To reduce the cost of therapy
To prevent pharmacological tolerance — best achieved at night when the patient is inactive (6-8 hours)
Because nitrates accumulate to toxic levels
To enhance the beta-blocker effect
check.explanation_ar: الاستخدام المستمر للنترات يحدث تحملاً دوائياً؛ فترة خلو 6-8 ساعات (ليلاً أفضل) تحفظ الفعالية — إلا إن كانت الذبحة الليلية مسيطرة فتُعطى النترات الطويلة نهاية اليوم.

key_terms.definition_ar: تدهور فعالية النترات مع الاستمرار؛ يُدار بفترة خلو 6-8 ساعات.
حاصر قناة If في العقدة الجيبية؛ يبطئ النبض دون تثبيط التقلص وآمن في قصور القلب.
مثبط تيار الصوديوم الداخلي المتأخر؛ يخف أعراض الذبحة دون تأثير ديناميكي كبير.

concepts.title: Revascularisation and Prognosis of Coronary Artery Disease
concepts.summary_ar: خيارات إعادة التروية (PCI/CABG) واستطباباتها بما فيها فائدة البقاء (LMS، ثلاثة أوعية، خلل البطين)، وإنذار المرض حسب الأوعية والوظيفة.

sections.heading: Revascularisation: Options and Indications
sections.body_text:
**Options: percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG).**

**Either CABG or PCI is indicated in the following groups of patients with stable angina pectoris:**
- **Patients with activity-limiting symptoms despite optimal medical therapy.**
- **Active patients who prefer PCI for improved quality of life compared to medical therapy.**
- **Those with anatomy for which revascularisation has a proven SURVIVAL benefit: LEFT MAIN STEM (LMS), THREE-VESSEL DISEASE, and LV SYSTOLIC DYSFUNCTION.**

**Prognosis (lecture closing):** the prognosis of CAD is related to the **number of diseased vessels and the degree of left ventricular dysfunction**:
- **Single-vessel disease with good LV function: 5-year survival > 90%.**
- **Severe LV dysfunction with extensive three-vessel disease: 5-year survival < 30% unless revascularisation is performed.**
- **Symptoms are a poor guide to prognosis** — spontaneous improvement in angina due to the **development of collateral vessels** is common; nevertheless, the **5-year mortality of patients with severe angina (CCS III or IV) is nearly double that of patients with mild symptoms.**
key_points: Indications: limiting symptoms despite OMT; patient preference (QoL); survival-benefit anatomy
Survival-benefit anatomy: left main stem, three-vessel disease, LV systolic dysfunction
Single-vessel + good LV: >90% 5-year survival; 3VD + severe LV dysfunction: <30% without revascularisation
Symptoms poorly reflect prognosis (collateral development); CCS III/IV doubles 5-year mortality

check.prompt: Which anatomical patterns carry a proven SURVIVAL benefit from revascularisation in stable CAD?
options: Single-vessel proximal LAD disease with normal LV function
Left main stem disease, three-vessel disease, and LV systolic dysfunction
Any patient with typical angina
Two-vessel disease with normal LV function
check.explanation_ar: فائدة البقاء تثبت للجذع الأيسر الرئيس وثلاثة أوعية وخلل الوظيفة الانقباضية للبطين؛ ما عدا ذلك تكون إعادة التروية لأعراض (OMT فاشل أو تفضيل المريض) لا للبقاء.

key_terms.definition_ar: تطعيم مجاورة الشريان التاجي بالأوعية (ثديية داخلية/ساقية) لتجاوز التضيقات.
تدخل تاجي عبر الجلد: بالون ودعامة عبر قسطرة لتوسيع الآفة الانسدادية.

flashcards.front_text: At what stenosis diameter does atherosclerosis become symptomatic, and which plaques cause acute events?
flashcards.back_text: Generally asymptomatic until stenosis exceeds 70-80% of luminal diameter (producing angina). Acute coronary/cerebrovascular syndromes are typically due to rupture or erosion of plaques leading to thrombosis — and these plaques may have LESS than 50% stenosis.
flashcards.explanation_ar: بلا أعراض حتى تجاوز التضيق 70-80% من قطر التجويف؛ والأحداث الحادة من تمزق/تآكل لويحات غالباً <50% مع خثرة.

flashcards.front_text: Name the histological sequence of atherosclerotic plaque progression.
flashcards.back_text: Endothelial dysfunction -> fatty streak (intracellular lipid/foam cells, silent) -> intermediate lesion (small extracellular lipid pools) -> atheroma (extracellular lipid core) -> fibroatheroma (matrix/SMC increase) -> vulnerable plaque (thin cap, necrotic core) -> ruptured/eroded plaque with thrombosis.
flashcards.explanation_ar: خلل البطانة ← خط دهني ← آفة وسيطة ← أثروما ← ليفي أثرومي ← لويحة هشة ← ممزقة/متآكلة مع خثرة.

flashcards.front_text: Match each CAD clinical problem to its pathology (Box 16.36).
flashcards.back_text: Stable angina = fixed atheromatous stenosis; unstable angina = dynamic obstruction from plaque rupture/erosion with thrombosis; MI = myocardial necrosis from acute occlusion; heart failure = dysfunction from infarction/ischaemia; arrhythmia = altered conduction; sudden death = ventricular arrhythmia, asystole or massive infarction.
flashcards.explanation_ar: المستقرة تضيق ثابت؛ غير المستقرة انسداد حركي بخثرة؛ الاحتشاء تنخر بانسداد حاد؛ والقصور واختلال النظم والموت المفاجئ تبعات.

flashcards.front_text: List the non-modifiable, modifiable and marker risk factors for CAD (Table 8.1).
flashcards.back_text: Non-modifiable: age, male sex, family history of premature CAD. Modifiable: hyperlipidaemia, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome, cigarette smoking, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, heavy alcohol intake. Markers: elevated Lp(a), hyperhomocysteinaemia, elevated hsCRP.
flashcards.explanation_ar: غير معدلة: عمر، ذكورة، قصة عائلية مبكرة؛ معدلة: شحوم، ضغط، سكري، متلازمة أيضية، تدخين، بدانة، خمول، كحول؛ وواسمات: Lp(a)، هوموسيستين، hsCRP.

flashcards.front_text: What determines myocardial oxygen demand and supply (Box 16.38)?
flashcards.back_text: Demand (cardiac work): heart rate, blood pressure, myocardial contractility, LV hypertrophy, valve disease. Supply (coronary blood flow, mainly in DIASTOLE): duration of diastole, coronary perfusion pressure (aortic diastolic minus coronary sinus/right atrial diastolic), coronary vasomotor tone, and oxygenation (haemoglobin, oxygen saturation).
flashcards.explanation_ar: الطلب: معدل، ضغط، تقلص، LVH، دسامات؛ والعرض (والتدفق بالانبساط أساساً): مدة الانبساط، ضغط التروية (انبساطي أبهري - انبساطي أيمن)، النقبض الوعائي التاجي، والخضاب والتشبع.

flashcards.front_text: What should the physical examination in suspected angina search for?
flashcards.back_text: It is frequently unremarkable, but look for: valve disease (particularly aortic); risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia); signs of LV dysfunction; other manifestations of arterial disease (carotid bruits, peripheral arterial disease); and conditions that may exacerbate angina (anaemia, thyrotoxicosis).
flashcards.explanation_ar: غالباً طبيعي؛ ابحث: دسامات (خصوصاً الأبهري)، عوامل خطر، علامات خلل بطين أيسر، لغط سباتي/مرض شرياني محيطي، وفقر دم أو تسمق درقي يفاقم الذبحة.

flashcards.front_text: Define coronary spasm/variant angina, Prinzmetal's angina, syndrome X and ANOCA.
flashcards.back_text: Variant angina: isolated vasospasm (<1% of cases) in angiographically normal coronaries; with transient ST elevation it is Prinzmetal's angina. Syndrome X: typical effort angina + objective ischaemia on stress testing + normal angiogram (many women; good prognosis; may respond to antianginals). ANOCA: angina with no obstructive CAD — one-third of patients, often microvascular disease.
flashcards.explanation_ar: التشنجي المعزول <1% بشرايين طبيعية؛ مع ارتفاع ST عابر = برنزميتال؛ متلازمة X: ذبحة نموذجية + نقص تروية موضوعي + تصوير طبيعي؛ وANOCA بلا انسداد إبكليلي (ثلث المرضى، وعائي دقيق).

flashcards.front_text: What distinguishes high-risk from low-risk stable angina (Box 16.41)?
flashcards.back_text: High risk: post-infarct angina, poor effort tolerance, ischaemia at low workload, left main or three-vessel disease, poor LV function. Low risk: predictable exertional angina, good effort tolerance, ischaemia only at high workload, one- or two-vessel disease, good LV function.
flashcards.explanation_ar: عالي: ذبحة بعد احتشاء، تحمل ضعيف، نقص تروية بحمل منخفض، جذع أيسر/ثلاثة أوعية، بطين ضعيف؛ ومنخفض: عكسها.

flashcards.front_text: What can the baseline ECG show in CCS and what does a normal ECG/echo mean?
flashcards.back_text: ECG: ST-depression, T-wave inversion, pathological Q-waves, ventricular hypertrophy, bundle branch block. A NORMAL ECG does NOT exclude ischaemia; a NORMAL resting echocardiogram does NOT exclude CAD.
flashcards.explanation_ar: انحراف ST هابط، انقلاب T، Q مرضية، LVH، حصار؛ والطبيعي في كليهما لا ينفي نقص التروية/المرض.

flashcards.front_text: What are the methods to induce and to detect ischaemia in stress testing?
flashcards.back_text: Induce: exercise (most physiological; adequate if >= 85% of age-predicted maximum heart rate [220 - age]) or pharmacological (dobutamine, adenosine, dipyridamole) for those who cannot exercise. Detect: stress ECG, stress echocardiography, nuclear study (SPECT/PET), CMR.
flashcards.explanation_ar: التحريض: جهد (85% من 220-العمر) أو دوائي (دوبوتامين/أدينوزين/ديبيريدامول)؛ والكشف: جهد كهربائي، جهد صدوي، نووي (SPECT/PET)، ورنين.

flashcards.front_text: Which patients are excluded from stress ECG, and what are its sensitivity/specificity?
flashcards.back_text: Exclude LVH, LBBB, resting ST-depression and digoxin users. General population: sensitivity 68%, specificity 70% (lower in low-risk persons). Best use: intermediate-risk patient with atypical history, or low-risk patient with typical history; high-risk patients usually go straight to invasive testing.
flashcards.explanation_ar: يُستثنى LVH وLBBB وانحراف راحة والديجوكسين؛ حساسية 68% ونوعية 70%؛ أمثل الحالات: متوسط الخطورة بقصة لانموذجية أو منخفضة بقصة نموذجية.

flashcards.front_text: How do stress echo and SPECT detect ischaemia, and what are their accuracies?
flashcards.back_text: Stress echo: new/worsening regional wall motion abnormality during stress; accuracy 80-90% for significant stenosis, superior to exercise ECG. SPECT: a perfusion defect present during stress but NOT at rest = reversible myocardial ischaemia.
flashcards.explanation_ar: صدى الجهد: اضطراب حركية جديد/أشد بدقة 80-90%؛ وSPECT: عيب تروية بالجهد يزول بالراحة = نقص تروية قابل للعكس.

flashcards.front_text: When is CT coronary angiography preferred over invasive catheterisation?
flashcards.back_text: CTCA is the non-invasive anatomical test best adopted for patients WITHOUT prior known CAD (Fig. 16.55 pathway after clinical assessment, bloods and ECG); for patients with KNOWN CAD, further stress imaging (echo, radionuclide or MR perfusion) rather than CTCA is recommended; invasive catheterisation for high-risk patients or when revascularisation is planned.
flashcards.explanation_ar: CTCA لغير معروفي المرض؛ ومعروفو المرض يكملون بتصوير جهد (صدى/نووي/رنين) لا CTCA؛ والقسطرة للخطورة العالية أو عند التخطيط لإعادة التروية.

flashcards.front_text: Summarise Box 16.42 advice to patients with stable angina.
flashcards.back_text: Do not smoke; aim for ideal body weight; take regular exercise (up to but not beyond the point of chest discomfort — may promote collateral vessels); avoid severe unaccustomed exertion and vigorous exercise after a heavy meal or in very cold weather; take sublingual nitrate prophylactically before exertion liable to provoke angina.
flashcards.explanation_ar: لا تدخن، وزن مثالي، تمرين منتظم دون عتبة الألم (يعزز الجوانب)، تجنب المجهول الشديد والجهد بعد الطعام الثقيل وفي الجو البارد، ونترات تحت لسانية وقائياً قبل الجهد.

flashcards.front_text: What are the first-line antihypertensives in CCD, and which diabetes drugs carry cardiovascular benefit?
flashcards.back_text: Hypertension (SBP >= 130 and/or DBP >= 80 mmHg): ACE inhibitors, ARBs or beta-blockers first line. Type 2 diabetes with CCD (HbA1c target < 7.0%): SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist for proven cardiovascular benefit.
flashcards.explanation_ar: ضغط ≥130/80: ACEi/ARB أو بيتا حاصر أولاً؛ وسكري نوع2 مع CCD: SGLT2i أو GLP-1RA بفائدة قلبية مثبتة (HbA1c <7%).

flashcards.front_text: What antiplatelet and statin therapy do all CCS patients receive?
flashcards.back_text: Aspirin 75 mg daily indefinitely (reduces MI risk); clopidogrel 75 mg daily is an equally effective alternative if aspirin is not tolerated. High-intensity statin at evidence-based doses regardless of baseline LDL; LDL-C goal < 1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) plus >= 50% reduction from baseline; add ezetimibe then bempedoic acid if unmet.
flashcards.explanation_ar: أسبرين 75 ملغ دائماً (أو كلوبيدوغريل عند التعذر)؛ وستاتين عالي الشدة مهما كان LDL بهدف <1.4 ملمول/ل و≥50% خفضاً، مع إزتيميب ثم بيمبيدويك عند القصور.

flashcards.front_text: How is a positive exercise ECG for ischaemia defined morphologically (Fig. 16.57 example)?
flashcards.back_text: Marked planar (horizontal) ST depression developing in the precordial leads during exercise (e.g., V5-V6 after 3 minutes of treadmill), often from a near-normal resting ECG — the example went on to critical three-vessel disease at angiography.
flashcards.explanation_ar: انحراف ST مستوٍ (أفقي) معلّم بالتوصيلات أمامية أثناء الجهد من رسم شبه طبيعي — المثال انتهى بثلاثة أوعية حرجة.

flashcards.front_text: How do nitrates work and how is tolerance avoided?
flashcards.back_text: Direct action on vascular smooth muscle: venous and arteriolar dilatation — lower preload/afterload (less demand) plus coronary vasodilatation (more supply). Sublingual GTN 400 mcg spray or 500-800 mcg tablet relieves attacks in 2-3 minutes. Long-acting: GTN patch 5-10 mg/day, buccal 1-5 mg QID, isosorbide dinitrate 10-20 mg TID, mononitrate 20-60 mg OD/BD. Avoid tolerance with a 6-8-hour nitrate-free period (best at night; end-of-day dosing if nocturnal angina).
flashcards.explanation_ar: توسع وريدي وشريني: خفض الحملين + توسع تاجي؛ GTN تحت لساني يريح خلال 2-3 دقائق؛ ويفاد التحمّل بفترة خلو 6-8 ساعات ليلاً.

flashcards.front_text: Which beta-blockers are preferred in angina and why must they not be stopped abruptly?
flashcards.back_text: Once-daily cardioselective preparations: slow-release metoprolol 60-200 mg daily or bisoprolol 5-15 mg daily (less bronchospasm; no coronary beta2 blockade that might aggravate vasospasm). Abrupt withdrawal causes the beta-blocker withdrawal syndrome — dangerous arrhythmias, worsening angina or MI.
flashcards.explanation_ar: ميتوبرولول مستر 60-200 أو بيسوبرولول 5-15 (انتقائيان مرة يومياً)؛ والقطع المفاجئ يحدث متلازمة انسحاب (نظميات خطرة وذبحة أسوأ واحتشاء).

flashcards.front_text: Compare the calcium channel blockers used in angina (Box 16.44).
flashcards.back_text: Dihydropyridines (nifedipine 5-20 mg TID — marked tachycardia, combine with beta-blocker; nicardipine 20-40 mg TID — less myocardial depression; amlodipine 2.5-10 mg daily — ultra-long-acting) vs non-DHP (verapamil 40-80 mg TID — constipation, anti-arrhythmic; diltiazem 60-120 mg TID — similar). Verapamil/diltiazem can be monotherapy (SA/AV slowing); all need care in poor LV function.
flashcards.explanation_ar: DHP: نيفي (تسرع — مع بيتا)، نيكاردب، أملودب طويل؛ وغير DHP: فيراباميل (إمساك وخواص نظمية) ودلتيازيم — تصلح وحدها؛ والجميع بحذر مع بطين ضعيف.

flashcards.front_text: What are the 'other' antianginal drugs and their mechanisms?
flashcards.back_text: Nicorandil 10-30 mg BD — potassium channel activator, arterial and venous vasodilator without nitrate tolerance. Ivabradine — If-channel antagonist of the sinus node, bradycardia without negative inotropy, safe in heart failure. Ranolazine — inhibits the late inward sodium current in coronary smooth muscle, reducing angina symptoms.
flashcards.explanation_ar: نيكوراندل (قناة بوتاسيوم، بلا تحمل نترات)؛ إيفابرادين (If جيبي، آمن في القصور)؛ رانولازين (تيار الصوديوم المتأخر).

flashcards.front_text: What are the indications for revascularisation in stable angina, and what determines prognosis?
flashcards.back_text: Indications: activity-limiting symptoms despite optimal medical therapy; active patients preferring PCI for quality of life; anatomy with proven survival benefit — left main stem, three-vessel disease, LV systolic dysfunction. Prognosis: number of diseased vessels + degree of LV dysfunction (single-vessel/good LV > 90% 5-year survival; severe LV dysfunction + 3VD < 30% without revascularisation); CCS III/IV nearly doubles 5-year mortality; symptoms are otherwise a poor guide (collaterals).
flashcards.explanation_ar: الاستطباب: أعراض مقيدة رغم العلاج الأمثل، تفضيل المريض، أو تشريح فائدة البقاء (LMS، ثلاثة أوعية، خلل البطين)؛ والإنذار بعدد الأوعية ووظيفة البطين.

mcqs.question_stem: A 55-year-old man presents with an acute STEMI. Angiography shows a culprit lesion with only 45% residual stenosis after thrombus aspiration. How can a subcritical stenosis have caused an infarction?
options: The measurement is wrong — infarctions require >70% stenosis
Plaque rupture or erosion with superimposed thrombosis rapidly converts a subcritical (often <50%) stenosis into total occlusion
All subcritical plaques occlude within a year
Microvascular disease alone explains it
mcqs.explanation_ar: الأحداث الحادة تنشأ من تمزق/تآكل لويحات دون 50% غالباً مع خثرة فائقة تُحدث انسداداً سريعاً؛ لا يلزم تضيق حرج مزمن — بعكس الذبحة المستقرة التي تحتاج >70-80%.

mcqs.question_stem: A 60-year-old with stable angina has tachycardia-controlled rate 110 bpm at rest. Which determinant of myocardial oxygen supply is being harmed by this tachycardia?
options: Coronary vasomotor tone only
Duration of diastole — coronary blood flow occurs mainly in diastole, which tachycardia shortens
Haemoglobin concentration
Aortic systolic pressure
mcqs.explanation_ar: التدفق التاجي يحدث بالانبساط أساساً؛ تسرّع القلب يقصّر الانبساط فيقل العرض بينما يرفع الطلب أيضاً — لذا حاصرات بيتا مزدوجة الفائدة.

mcqs.question_stem: A 52-year-old woman has exertional chest tightness, 2 mm horizontal ST depression on exercise ECG, yet angiography shows smooth normal coronary arteries. What is the diagnosis and its outlook?
options: Syndrome X — good prognosis, may respond to antianginal therapy
Left main stem disease requiring CABG
NSTEMI requiring immediate PCI
Aortic stenosis
mcqs.explanation_ar: متلازمة X: ذبحة نموذجية + نقص تروية موضوعي بالجهد + شرايين طبيعية؛ شائعة لدى النساء، مآل جيد، وقد تستجيب للمضادة للذبحة — وينظر أيضاً في آلية ANOCA الوعائية الدقيقة.

mcqs.question_stem: Which patient with chest pain is at highest risk on Box 16.41 stratification?
options: Predictable exertional angina with good effort tolerance and single-vessel disease
Post-infarct angina with ischaemia at low workload and poor LV function
Ischaemia only at high workload with good LV function
Two-vessel disease with good effort tolerance
mcqs.explanation_ar: ذبحة ما بعد الاحتشاء مع نقص تروية بحمل منخفض وخلل بطين = عالي الخطورة (مع جذع أيسر/ثلاثة أوعية)؛ والبقية منخفضة.

mcqs.question_stem: A 58-year-old with LBBB and suspected angina needs ischaemia testing. Which modality is appropriate?
options: Exercise ECG alone
Stress echocardiography or imaging-based stress (SPECT/CMR) — LBBB, LVH, resting ST depression and digoxin exclude exercise-ECG interpretation
No testing is possible
Daily 12-lead ECG
mcqs.explanation_ar: LBBB وLVH وانحراف الراحة والديجوكسين تُخرج من تفسير جهد التخطيط؛ البديل: صدى الجهد أو التصوير النووي/الرنين — وصدى الجهد أدق (80-90%).

mcqs.question_stem: In SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging, what finding constitutes evidence of reversible ischaemia?
options: A defect present at rest that persists at stress
A perfusion defect present during stress but NOT at rest
Global uniform uptake at stress
An infarct pattern of uptake
mcqs.explanation_ar: عيب تروية بالجهد يزول بالراحة = نقص تروية عكوس؛ الثابت بالحالتين ندقة/احتشاء.

mcqs.question_stem: A 61-year-old with CCS, type 2 diabetes and BP 144/88 mmHg is on aspirin. What additional risk-factor pharmacotherapy does the lecture mandate?
options: SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist for the diabetes, ACE inhibitor/ARB or beta-blocker for the hypertension, and a high-intensity statin regardless of baseline LDL
Insulin only for the diabetes
No statin if LDL is normal
Diuretic as sole antihypertensive
mcqs.explanation_ar: سكري CCD: SGLT2i أو GLP-1RA؛ ضغط ≥130/80: ACEi/ARB أو بيتا؛ وستاتين عالي الشدة مهما كان LDL بهدف <1.4 ملمول/ل و≥50% خفضاً.

mcqs.question_stem: A patient on isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg twice daily reports returning angina after 2 weeks. What is the likely explanation and fix?
options: True allergy to nitrates — stop all vasodilators
Pharmacological nitrate tolerance — build in a 6-8-hour nitrate-free period (best at night; asymmetric end-of-day dosing if nocturnal angina)
Metabolic acidosis
The dose was too low — triple it immediately
mcqs.explanation_ar: التحمل الدوائي للنترات هو التفسير الأشيع؛ الحل فترة خلو 6-8 ساعات (ليلية عادة)، أو إعطاء الجرعة الطويلة نهاية اليوم إن كانت الذبحة ليلية.

mcqs.question_stem: A 68-year-old with angina has COPD, cannot tolerate beta-blockers, and has poor LV function. Which antianginal choices fit best?
options: Nifedipine alone at high dose
Diltiazem cautiously only if LV function acceptable, otherwise consider ivabradine (if sinus rhythm), ranolazine or nicorandil — with short-acting GTN for relief
Propranolol
Verapamil with a beta-blocker
mcqs.explanation_ar: غير DHP خيار عدم تحمل البيتا لكنه مثبط تقلص (حذر مع البطين الضعيف)؛ والبدائل الآمنة: إيفابرادين (جيبي، آمن قصورياً)، رانولازين، نيكوراندل، مع GTN قصير للنجدة؛ الجمع بيتا+فيراباميل ممنوع.

mcqs.question_stem: Angiography in a symptomatic patient shows distal left main stenosis of 70% with LV EF 40%. What is the indication for revascularisation here?
options: Patient preference only — no survival benefit exists
Anatomy with a proven survival benefit (left main stem disease with LV systolic dysfunction) — revascularisation is indicated
No indication unless symptoms fail three drugs
PCI is contraindicated in left main disease
mcqs.explanation_ar: الجذع الأيسر وثلاثة الأوعية وخلل البطين = تشريح فائدة البقاء؛ إعادة التروية مستطبَة لا تنتظر فشل الأدوية (مع الأعراض المقيدة أو التفضيل كدوافع أخرى).

clinical_cases.title: New-Onset Exertional Chest Pain: The Stable Angina Pathway
clinical_cases.scenario: A 57-year-old schoolteacher presents to the outpatient clinic with 3 months of central chest tightness on climbing two flights of stairs, reliably relieved by 2-3 minutes of rest. This case walks the full lecture pathway from typical-angina recognition through baseline tests, stress testing strategy, and the evidence-based preventive package — the essence of chronic coronary syndrome assessment.

vignette.chief_complaint: Exertional central chest tightness for 3 months
vignette.history: Pain is central, 'tight', radiates to the left jaw, provoked by two flights of stairs or walking against a cold wind, relieved by rest in 2-3 minutes; never at rest; no syncope. Smoker 20 pack-years; father had MI at 55; no diabetes known. On no medications.
vignette.exam: Comfortable; BMI 29. Right carotid bruit; no radiofemoral delay; heart sounds normal with no murmur; chest clear; no oedema; palpable dorsalis pedis pulses both sides.
vignette.imaging: Resting ECG: sinus rhythm, normal (no ST/T changes, no LVH, no Q waves). Resting echocardiography: EF 58%, no regional wall-motion abnormality, mild LVH, no significant valve disease. Exercise ECG: achieved 92% of age-predicted maximum heart rate (adequate test); 1.5-2 mm horizontal ST depression in V5-V6 at stage 2 with chest tightness — POSITIVE test with good effort tolerance.

steps.prompt: Is this typical angina, and why do the normal ECG and echo not reassure?
options: Atypical pain — no further testing needed
Typical angina (exertional substernal tightness, relieved by rest); a normal ECG does NOT exclude ischaemia and a normal resting echo does NOT exclude CAD
Definitely non-cardiac because the exam is normal
Unstable angina requiring admission
steps.explanation_ar: الثلاثية النموذجية (خلف القص بالجهد، يزول بالراحة) = ذبحة نموذجية؛ والتخطيط والصدى السكونيان الطبيعيان لا ينفيان — بل يوجّهان للجهد، مع البحث عن مفاقمات (فقر دم، درق) وعلامات دسامية/شريانية (لغط سباتي هنا).

steps.prompt: Was exercise ECG the right first stress test here, and why was the test 'adequate'?
options: No — he should have gone straight to invasive angiography

Yes — intermediate-risk patient, interpretable baseline ECG; the test is adequate because >= 85% of the age-predicted maximum heart rate (220 - age) was achieved; functional capacity carries prognostic value
No — pharmacological stress was mandatory above age 55
Exercise ECG is only for asymptomatic screening
steps.explanation_ar: خطر متوسط + أساس قابل للتأويل = جهد كهربائي مناسب؛ وبلوغ ≥85% من (220-57) يجعله كافياً؛ الانحراف الأفقي القمي في المرحلة 2 إيجابي، وسعة الجهد ذات قيمة إنذارية.

steps.prompt: Given a positive test with good effort tolerance and no high-risk features, what is the recommended next anatomical step?
options: CT coronary angiography — the pathway test for patients WITHOUT known CAD
Immediate CABG
Repeat exercise ECG weekly
Discharge with GTN only
steps.explanation_ar: لمريض غير معروف المرض وفق مخطط 16.55: بعد التقييم والتحاليل والتخطيط والجهد يُطلب CTCA لتشريح الشرايين؛ والقسطرة تُحفظ للخطورة العالية أو التخطيط لإعادة التروية.

steps.prompt: Regardless of the CTCA result, which preventive drug package starts today?
options: Aspirin 75 mg indefinitely, high-intensity statin (goal LDL-C < 1.4 mmol/L and >= 50% reduction), antihypertensive (ACE inhibitor/ARB or beta-blocker — BP >= 130/80), plus sublingual GTN for attacks/prophylaxis; diabetes drugs with CV benefit if T2DM confirmed
GTN as needed only
Clopidogrel plus furosemide
No drugs until angiography
steps.explanation_ar: الحزمة: أسبرين 75 دائماً، ستاتين عالي الشدة بهدف <1.4 و≥50%، علاج الضغط (≥130/80: ACEi/ARB أو بيتا)، GTN قصير للنجدة والوقاية قبل الجهد، وSGLT2i/GLP-1RA عند تثبيت السكري — مع نصائح 16.42.

clinical_cases.debriefing_ar: الحالة تطبق مسار الذبحة المستقرة كاملاً: ألم نموذجي ثلاثي الخصائص مع عوامل خطر (تدخين، قصة عائلية، ما قبل السكري، LDL 4.3، ضغط ≥130/80) ولغط سباتي (مرض شرياني منتشر). التخطيط والصدى السكونيان طبيعيان — وهذا لا ينفي؛ فجهد التخطيط (بلوغ 92% من 220-العمر = كافٍ) أظهر انحرافاً أفقياً قمياً مع الألم. الخطوة التشريحية CTCA لغير معروف المرض، وتُحفظ القسطرة للخطورة العالية/إعادة التروية. العلاج يبدأ فوراً: أسبرين، ستاتين عالي الشدة (هدف <1.4 و≥50%)، علاج الضغط، GTN قصير مع النصائح الوقائية، وSGLT2i/GLP-1RA عند تأكيد السكري. الدروس: 1) سلبية السكون لا تعني شيئاً في الذبحة؛ 2) كفاية اختبار الجهد تعتمد على 85% من النبض الأقصى المتوقع؛ 3) CTCA لغير المعروفين والقسطرة للخطورة العالية؛ 4) الوقاية الثانوية لا تنتظر نتيجة التشريح.

clinical_cases.title: Symptomatic Three-Vessel Disease: The Revascularisation Decision
clinical_cases.scenario: A 66-year-old former security guard remains limited by angina (CCS III) despite maximal tolerated medical therapy. His CT coronary angiogram shows extensive three-vessel disease with reduced LV function. The multidisciplinary meeting must apply the lecture's revascularisation indications and prognosis data to choose between CABG, PCI and continued medical therapy.

vignette.chief_complaint: Activity-limiting angina despite optimal medical therapy (CCS III)
vignette.history: Angina for 4 years; now chest tightness after 50 metres. On aspirin 75 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, bisoprolol 10 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, isosorbide mononitrate 60 mg BD (with nitrate-free nights) and GTN prn. Prior NSTEMI 3 years ago (PCI to RCA). Diabetes on metformin; ex-smoker.
vignette.exam: Trace ankle oedema; apex displaced 2 cm laterally; S4 gallop; no murmurs; chest clear; carotids equal without bruits; foot pulses present.
vignette.imaging: CT coronary angiography: heavy calcification; proximal 80% LAD, 70% circumflex, 90% ostial RCA (chronic total occlusion with collateral filling); distal left main 50%. Invasive angiography with ventriculography: EF 42% with anterior hypokinesis. FFR/CABG heart-team discussion pending.

steps.prompt: Which lecture indication(s) for revascularisation does this patient satisfy?
options: None — he is already on two antianginals
All three: activity-limiting symptoms despite optimal medical therapy; anatomy with proven survival benefit (extensive three-vessel disease with LV systolic dysfunction); (patient preference pending)
Patient preference only
Urgent indication for fibrinolysis
steps.explanation_ar: أعراض مقيدة (CCS III) رغم العلاج الأمثل + تشريح فائدة البقاء (ثلاثة أوعية مع EF 42%)؛ وهذان استطبابان مستقلان يكفيان منفردَين، والثالث تفضيل المريض.
hints: EF 42% وثلاثة أوعية تصنعان أي استطباب؟

steps.prompt: What prognosis data justify offering revascularisation rather than continuing medical therapy alone?
options: Symptoms always predict prognosis accurately

Severe LV dysfunction with extensive three-vessel disease carries a 5-year survival < 30% unless revascularised (vs > 90% for single-vessel disease with good LV); CCS III/IV nearly doubles 5-year mortality
Revascularisation cures diabetes
Medical therapy is always superior in diabetics
steps.explanation_ar: الأوعية الثلاثة مع خلل البطين الشديد تنجو <30% خلال 5 سنوات دون إعادة تروية مقابل >90% لوعاء واحد بوظيفة جيدة؛ والذبحة الشديدة (III/IV) تضاعف الوفاة تقريباً — والأعراض بحد ذاتها دليل إنذار فقير (الجوانب تحسّن الأعراض دون الأوعية).

steps.prompt: Which antianginal intensification options remain per the 2024 ESC stepwise recommendations before/alongside revascularisation?
options: None — beta-blocker and CCB are already maximal
Combine beta-blocker + DHP-CCB if not already combined (he is), and add long-acting nitrate or ranolazine as add-on (IIa B) — nicorandil, ivabradine or ranolazine as alternatives
Stop all antianginals before surgery
Add verapamil to bisoprolol
steps.explanation_ar: هو أصلاً على بيتا+DHP-CCB ونترات طويلة؛ البدائل الإضافية: رانولازين أو نيكوراندل أو إيفابرادين (IIa B)؛ والجمع بيتا+فيراباميل/دلتيازيم ممنوع (بطء شديد وتثبيط تقلص).

steps.prompt: His LDL is 2.9 mmol/L on atorvastatin 40 mg. What does the 2024 lipid ladder require?
options: Accept 2.9 mmol/L — he is on a statin

Uptitrate to high-intensity atorvastatin 80 mg (or rosuvastatin 20-40 mg) toward LDL-C < 1.4 mmol/L with >= 50% reduction; add ezetimibe if unmet; then bempedoic acid; also intensify diabetes therapy with an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 RA
Stop the statin because of diabetes
Switch to a fibrate only
steps.explanation_ar: الهدف <1.4 ملمول/ل مع خفض ≥50%: تصعيد الأتورفاستاتين إلى 80 (أو روزوفاستاتين 20-40) ثم إزتيميب ثم بيمبيدويك عند القصور؛ وإضافة SGLT2i أو GLP-1RA للسكري (HbA1c 7.6% > الهدف 7%).

clinical_cases.debriefing_ar: حالة قرار إعادة التروية في المتلازمة المزمنة: CCS III رغم (أسبرين + ستاتين + بيتا + DHP-CCB + نترات طويلة بفترة خلو) مع ثلاثة أوعية (LAD 80%، Cx 70%، RCA 90% مُسدّ كلياً مزمن) وEF 42% وذرع أيسر 50%. الاستطبابات مكتملة: أعراض مقيدة رغم OMT + تشريح فائدة البقاء (3VD + خلل البطين)؛ وبيانات الإنذار (<30% بقاء 5 سنوات بلا إعادة تروية مقابل >90% لوعاء واحد بوظيفة جيدة) تدعم التدخل، مع مضاعفة الذبحة III/IV للوفاة. وفق 2024: تُكثف الأدوية المضادة للذبحة (رانولازين/نيكوراندل/إيفابرادين) وتُشدّد الدهون (هدف <1.4 و≥50% بإزتيميب ثم بيمبيدويك) والسكري (SGLT2i/GLP-1RA). الدروس: 1) استطبابا الأعراض والتشريح مستقلان؛ 2) الأعراض مؤشر إنذار فقير (الجوانب) لكن شدتها (III/IV) تنبئية؛ 3) حظر جمع بيتا مع فيراباميل/دلتيازيم؛ 4) سلم الدهون المتدرج لا يتوقف عند الستاتين وحده.
